selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What main lesson is this passage trying to teach about prayer and avoiding major sins?
questions.answer: It teaches that praying and staying away from major sins are basic duties that fit human nature and the purpose for which people were created.

questions.question: In the comparison, what kind of situation were the two soldiers in?
questions.answer: They were serving during a time of full military call-up and were together in one unit.

questions.question: How is the first soldier described?
questions.answer: He is described as disciplined, careful about his duty, and properly trained.

questions.question: How is the second soldier described?
questions.answer: He is described as inexperienced and mainly concerned with himself.

questions.question: What did the careful soldier focus on most?
questions.answer: He focused on preparing himself and doing his part in the fighting.

questions.question: Why did the careful soldier not worry much about food and supplies?
questions.answer: He understood that providing those things was the responsibility of the government.

questions.question: Besides training and fighting, what small support tasks did the careful soldier still do?
questions.answer: He helped with simple camp duties like preparing cookware, cleaning eating tools, and bringing them where needed.

questions.question: When asked what he was doing, how did the careful soldier understand those chores?
questions.answer: He saw them as service connected to the state, not as a personal job just to earn food.

questions.question: What does his answer tell us about how he viewed his daily chores?
questions.answer: It shows he viewed them as part of obedience and responsibility, not as chasing personal gain.

questions.question: According to the passage, what are people asked to understand through the soldier comparison?
questions.answer: They are asked to understand that the daily prayers and staying away from grave sins are natural and proper duties for human beings.

questions.question: Where were the two soldiers placed?
questions.answer: They were in the same regiment during a public military mobilization.

questions.question: What personal quality made the first soldier act differently from the second?
questions.answer: He had a strong sense of responsibility and took his duty seriously.

questions.question: What was the second soldier mainly thinking about?
questions.answer: He was mainly thinking about his own food and provisions.

questions.question: What belief guided the first soldier’s calm attitude about being fed and equipped?
questions.answer: He believed the authorities would take care of his basic needs.

questions.question: How far did that trust go if he became too weak or sick?
questions.answer: He believed they would even care for him very closely if necessary.

questions.question: What did the first soldier know was his own main responsibility?
questions.answer: His own responsibility was to prepare himself well and take part in the battle.

questions.question: Did the first soldier completely ignore supply-related work? Explain.
questions.answer: No. He still helped with certain practical tasks when they were part of his assigned work.

questions.question: Based on the whole comparison, what kind of person is being praised?
questions.answer: A person who knows his duty, acts responsibly, and trusts the One in charge for his needs is being praised.

questions.question: What two actions are linked together as part of true human responsibility in this passage?
questions.answer: Performing the prescribed prayers and avoiding serious sins.

questions.question: Why does the passage use a comparison with soldiers?
questions.answer: It uses a familiar example to make the lesson about duty, trust, and obedience easier to understand.

questions.question: What was special about the time when the story happened?
questions.answer: It was a time when people had been called up generally for military service.

questions.question: What can be understood from calling one soldier “conscientious”?
questions.answer: It means he was reliable, careful, and committed to doing what he was supposed to do.

questions.question: What can be understood from calling the other soldier “self-centred”?
questions.answer: It means he mostly cared about himself instead of the larger mission or shared duty.

questions.question: Why did the dutiful soldier not make obtaining food his main concern?
questions.answer: He knew that his needs would be provided by those in charge, while his own duty was something else.
